summary: Explains that a BGP speaker can apply RPKI origin validation to routes it sends as well as routes it receives. For such export checks, the classification should use the effective origin AS, which can be changed by features like removing private ASes or confederation handling. It updates RFC 6811 and is standards-track.

eli5.summary: Before handing out directions, a router can check that the destination really belongs to the claimed owner. This document says routers can do that check on outgoing announcements too, looking at who will really appear as the owner.

questions: can rpki origin validation be applied to bgp export
what is the effective origin as
what is rpki origin validation on bgp export
does origin validation apply to outbound bgp routes
subtitle: Check route origins on the routes a BGP router sends out, using the origin AS that will actually be announced.

tldr.problem: RPKI origin validation is usually applied to routes a router receives, but outbound routes can have their origin AS changed by configuration, so checking the stored route can give the wrong answer.
tldr.mechanism: A validating BGP speaker applies origin validation in egress policy too, using the effective origin AS: the origin of the UPDATE as it will be sent after removing private ASes, confederation handling and similar changes.
tldr.outcome: It updates RFC 6811 to make this explicit and adds no new security considerations beyond RFC 6811 and RFC 8481.

today: RFC 8893 is a Proposed Standard published in September 2020. It updates RFC 6811 and has not been obsoleted or updated.

sections.title: Outbound Origin Validation
sections.content:
This document does not change the protocol or semantics of RFC 6811, BGP prefix origin validation. It highlights an important use case: origin validation in external BGP (eBGP) egress policies, and how to implement it correctly there.

It updates RFC 6811 by clarifying that implementations must use the effective origin AS to determine the Origin Validation state when applying egress policy.
sections.eli5: Routers already check where announcements come from when they arrive. This note says they can check the ones they send out, too.

sections.title: The Effective Origin AS
sections.content:
The effective origin AS is the Route Origin ASN of the UPDATE that will be sent to neighboring BGP speakers. It is decided by the configuration and outbound policy of the speaker, so it can differ from the origin of the route stored in the RIB.

Removal of private ASes, confederation, migration and other AS_PATH modifications can change it. A validating BGP speaker MUST apply Route Origin Validation policy semantics after applying any egress configuration and policy, and any AS_PATH modification that changes the effective origin AS MUST be taken into account.
sections.eli5: The name on the envelope is what counts, not the name in the filing cabinet. If the name gets changed on the way out, check the new one.

sections.title: Egress Processing
sections.content:
BGP implementations that support RPKI-based origin validation MUST provide the same policy configuration primitives for decisions based on validation state in ingress, redistribution and egress policies. In egress policy, validation state MUST be determined using the effective origin AS of the route as it will (or would) be announced to the peer.

The RFC says egress handling can protect outbound eBGP more robustly than relying only on ingress or redistribution being configured and working correctly, which supports the robustness principle.
sections.eli5: A router gets the same set of checking tools for incoming, passed-along and outgoing routes. For outgoing ones it checks the name that will really be sent.

sections.title: Operational Considerations
sections.content:
Policies can be complex, and the effective origin AS may not be easy to determine until the outbound policies have run. It SHOULD be possible to specify a selective origin validation policy that is applied after any existing non-validating outbound policies.

An implementation SHOULD be able to list announcements that were not sent to a peer, for example because they were marked Invalid, as long as the router still has them in memory.
sections.eli5: Do the checking last, after the other changes are done. And keep a list of what was held back, so people can see what happened.
